title: veyq-subtree manifest
description: The manifest of a veyq node-subtree download (ADR 0082): the plaintext tree of one node and everything under it. Version 2 (written today) sits at `.veyq/manifest.json` beside the tree, which the store-only ZIP holds as itself: a directory per node that holds others, each file under its own name, every name made safe for every file system. Version 1 (still read, never written) sat at `manifest.json` with every payload under `data/<node id>/`. Core owns the envelope, the node shape and the payload shape; a node's `content` is opaque to core beyond its `type` and `schema`, and its shape is the application's, in that application's own schema `contracts/export/<application>/content.schema.json` (the `<application>` part of `content.type`), which its `validateContent` checks before an import writes anything. Readers ignore unknown fields and refuse a `version` newer than they know. Beyond what JSON Schema can say, a reader caps the tree at 200000 nodes and a depth of 100, the manifest at 128 MiB, and refuses a payload path that does not lie at or under its node's `path`.

version.description: Format version. Bumped only by a change an older reader would misread; an additive field never bumps it. 2: the tree layout with `.veyq/manifest.json` (ADR 0082 decision 3). 1: the `data/<id>/` layout, read for archives written before it.

exportedAt.description: Client clock at export, RFC 3339 UTC.

appVersion.description: The platform major the exporting web client was built for (informational; ADR 0085 decision 1), e.g. `0`. Never the precise release: the client that writes it is served before any login, and ADR 0057 decision 4 keeps the release off that surface. A reader must not rely on its shape; archives written before 2026-10-16 carry `dev`.

options.description: Version 1 only: the options chosen at export. A version 2 writer omits it (there are no options) and a reader ignores it.

includeLocation.description: False when GPS and place data were left out of the manifest at export time; the fields are then absent, not null.

applications.description: Version 2: every application whose kinds the tree carries, with the version of its content schema the writer wrote. A reader lists, before it writes anything, the nodes of an application it does not have and of one whose content is newer than it reads (ADR 0082 decision 9). Each `id` appears once.

id.description: The application's id: the part of a `content.type` before the dot (e.g. `memories`).

contentSchema.description: The highest `content.schema` of this application's kinds in the tree.

archivePath.description: Version 2: a path inside the ZIP, relative, `/`-separated, the node's place in the tree (`Trip 2025/Lisbon/IMG_0412.jpg`). Every segment is a safe archive name (ADR 0082 decision 3: no `/` or `\`, not `.` or `..`, no control character, no Windows reserved name, no trailing dot or space, bounded, clashes numbered `Name (2)`), and nothing lies under `.veyq/`, which holds the manifest. A label, never an identity: the manifest, not the path, says which node a payload belongs to.

archivePathV1.description: Version 1: `data/<node.id>/<file name>`. The importer reads only paths it finds in the manifest and refuses any that leaves data/ (no `..`, no absolute path, no backslash).

path.description: Where the bytes are: an `archivePath` in version 2, an `archivePathV1` in version 1.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the stored bytes; the importer verifies it while streaming.

modifiedAt.description: Optional: the file's modified time at export, in milliseconds since the epoch, for a kind that keeps one; restored on import.

id.description: Archive-local id, unique in this manifest (`n1`, `n2`, ...). Not a veyq node id; carries no meaning outside the file.

kind.description: The node kind: core's FOLDER or an application's (contracts/platform/kinds/). An importing build that lacks the kind skips that node and its subtree and reports it.

name.description: The node's name as veyq shows it. Its archive path's last segment is this name made safe, so the two may differ.

path.description: Version 2: where the node sits in the archive. A node that holds others is a directory and its payloads lie in it; a node of a kind that IS one file is that file, its one payload at this very path. The exported node's own path is its safe name. Required in version 2.

cover.description: The node's cover image (core's COVER attachment), if any.

metadata.description: The kind's plaintext node metadata that is not content. Open: unknown keys are ignored.

content.description: What the kind's export hook supplied; absent for a node that has none (a FOLDER).

children.description: In the order the source tree showed them.

content.description: What the kind's export hook supplied, opaque to core beyond these two fields: its shape is the application's, `contracts/export/<application>/content.schema.json` for the `<application>` part of `type`. Open: core neither lists the types nor checks the rest.

type.description: `<application>.<name>`; the importing kind's hook dispatches on it, and its application part names the entry of `applications`.

schema.description: The kind's own content schema version; the hook refuses a newer one.

nodeV1.description: A version 1 node: the common shape, every child a version 1 node.

nodeV2.description: A version 2 node: the common shape plus its `path`, every child a version 2 node.
